government.note: Presidential system under the 1994 Constitution as amended by the November 1996 referendum. The President appoints the Prime Minister and can call elections and referendums and dissolve both chambers. The 1996 referendum moved the presidential election due in 1999 to 2001; the 2004 referendum removed the two-term limit; the 2022 referendum reimposed a two-term limit only for newly elected presidents, extended the parliamentary term to five years and made the All-Belarusian People's Assembly a constitutional body. After the 1996 referendum a new House of Representatives was assembled from deputies loyal to the President, while about sixty members of the former Supreme Soviet who rejected the new constitution continued to meet and were recognised by much of the international community.

system.note: 110 deputies elected in single-member constituencies (the 2000 and 2004 elections needed further rounds in some seats). Four-year term until the 2022 amendments set five years. The House in office on 1 January 2000 was the one assembled after the November 1996 referendum from deputies of the former Supreme Soviet loyal to the President, not elected as such.

system.note: Eight members for each of the six oblasts and Minsk city, elected by deputies of the regional councils (two rounds if necessary), plus eight appointed by the President. Established after the 1996 referendum. Term follows the House (four years until the 2022 amendments). Party composition on 1 January 2000 is not recorded in the fetched sources.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Estimate for a non-competitive system, not a measured vote. Anchored on Lukashenko's 80.6% in the 1994 run-off and 77.4% in 2001 (official results) for support of the presidential camp (statist), and on the 1995 Supreme Council election, in which the Party of Communists (43 seats) and the Agrarian Party (33) were the largest parties and the United Civic Party and social democrats won a few seats. The government in 2000 was formed by the President without a party base.
